label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 8
knowledgePattern: Recover a linear remainder from two polynomial values
solution:
Dividing p(x) by (x−2)(x+3) leaves a remainder of degree below two. Write p(x)=(x−2)(x+3)q(x)+ax+b.

At x = 2 and x = −3 the product term vanishes, giving 2a+b=7 and −3a+b=−8. Subtraction gives a=3, then b=1.

Hence p(x)=(x−2)(x+3)q(x)+3x+1, with q a polynomial. Answer D.

hints.title: Write the remainder with unknown coefficients
hints.body: Dividing by (x−2)(x+3) leaves a remainder of degree less than 2. Write that remainder as ax+b.
hints.recap: The remainder has lower degree than the divisor.
hints.pitfall: The quotient can stay unknown; you do not need to find it.
hints.pause: Write the polynomial as divisor times quotient plus your remainder.

recall.reminder: The remainder has lower degree than the divisor.

hints.title: Use the two given inputs
hints.body: Substitute x=2 and x=−3 into your expression for p(x). The product with the quotient disappears at both inputs.
hints.recap: At a zero of the divisor, the polynomial value equals the remainder value.
hints.pitfall: Use the given value for each input with its correct sign.
